### B2 — Page container + route

Create `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` — a thin container: reads `recentlyViewedIds`
off A4's `useRecentlyViewedHistory()` (**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08** — was `useEinstein().
getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)`, per "Interim data source" in §2;
`getRecommendations` is not called at all by this page in the interim build), fetches real product
data for the stored ID list via `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` — **capped at 24, not the rail's
5-item slice** (was described as "full, uncapped" before the `getProducts` 24-ID-per-request limit
was discovered during Phase 1; the storage layer itself is now also capped at 24 for the same
reason, so this page genuinely does receive its full available history, just one that's bounded
by design rather than literally unbounded) — maps through **a new mapper (see
below — not A3's)**, renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`, owns the `react-intl` copy, and sets
`getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed'` per the four existing page precedents. Add
`RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE = '/recently-viewed'` to `overrides/app/constants/index.ts`. Add the route to
`routes.tsx`.

**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-07 — "maps through A3's mapper" was wrong; a new mapper is needed, but no new
data-fetching architecture is.** Jasmijn's newest SFCC-84 comment specifies the Full History card's
default state as *"image, name, badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon"* — i.e. exactly the
`plp` variation's existing, already-shipped shape (B1's hover-behaviour cross-check above confirms
the rest). **A3's mapper cannot feed this**: by its own docblock it deliberately returns only
`{id, href, name, primaryImage, currentPrice}` — no `originalPrice`, no `images` — because A2/A3 were
scoped for the rail's image-only design, not the page's full card.

**Still fully valid after the 2026-09-08 data-source swap above — restated, not re-derived.** This
finding was originally verified against Einstein's `fetchRecProductDetails`, which internally calls
`getProducts` with `allImages: true` / `perPricebook: true` / `expand: [...]`. The interim
`recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` calls the **same underlying Shopper Products endpoint with the same
flags** (see §2) — just triggered by our own tracked ID list instead of Einstein's rec list — so
every field this finding relies on (`imageGroups`, `tieredPrices`) is equally present either way. The
was/now-pricing and multi-image work below was never actually Einstein-specific; it was already
correct once the underlying `getProducts` call is right, regardless of who supplies the ID list.

**Verified 2026-09-07 (pre-dates the interim-source revision; kept as the technical record), directly
against source, not assumed:** the data those extra fields need is already flowing through the
*same* underlying Shopper Products call both A3's original Einstein-sourced design and this page
consume. `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails`
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505`) does a real Shopper
Products `getProducts` call — `allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: ['prices',
'promotions', 'images', 'variations', ...]` — and merges the full result as `{...rec, ...product,
productId, image: {...}}`. So the object any mapper here receives already carries
`product.imageGroups` (real multi-image galleries — the same field
`productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` already reads off a Search hit) and
`product.tieredPrices` (per-pricebook pricing). Base SFCC ships a ready-made utility for exactly
this shape — `getPriceData` (`app/utils/product-utils.js:123`) — which already derives `listPrice`
(the max of `tieredPrices`, i.e. "was"), the current tiered `price` ("now"), and `isOnSale =
currentPrice < listPrice`. **Neither A3 nor `productListCardMapper.ts` calls it; both explicitly set
`originalPrice: undefined` instead, with comments claiming the data or the logic isn't available.**
That claim is now known to be inaccurate for the Einstein pipeline specifically — raised as Open
Question 16 rather than silently rewritten into A3, since A3 is already-committed, scored work and
changing its behaviour now is a distinct decision from documenting this plan correctly.

**Consequence (restated 2026-09-08 for the interim source, same conclusion either way):** no
*second* product-detail fetch is needed on top of the one `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` already
makes (originally written as "on top of what `getRecommendations`/`fetchRecProductDetails` already
does," back when Einstein was still the assumed source — the underlying point is unchanged: one
`getProducts`-shaped call, correctly flagged, already carries everything needed). What's needed is a
**new mapper**, `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` (added to the file manifest),
that:
- calls base `getPriceData(product)` and maps `listPrice`/`price` to `originalPrice`/`currentPrice`,
  only setting `originalPrice` when `isOnSale` is true — a not-on-sale product should not render a
  crossed-out price identical to its current one;
- reuses (or ports, if `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own types don't line up — decide at
  implementation time) `selectGalleryImages`'s image-group-picking logic against
  `product.imageGroups`;
- produces `variation: 'plp'`-shaped props (badge, size chips, hover-swap image), not A3's narrow
  `recentlyViewed` shape.

**Honest caveat, not provable from code alone:** whether `tieredPrices` actually comes back with
more than one entry depends on Zimmermann's live SFCC pricebook configuration — with only one active
pricebook, `getPriceData` will correctly compute `isOnSale: false` every time (correct behaviour,
not a bug), but this can't be fully confirmed working until checked against a real on-sale product
in a running environment — same "verify in the running app" discipline as A1/A6/B3 elsewhere in
this plan.

**Empty state (DECIDED 2026-09-06 — from codebase precedent, not invented).** SFCC-84 has no
empty-state AC, and the house pattern never renders nothing: `EmptyCart`, `EmptySearchResults` and
`empty-wishlist` all render heading + copy + CTA. `EmptyCart` is the near-exact analogue (a personal
page that can legitimately be empty) and branches its copy on `isRegistered` — **the same value A4's
gate hook already computes**.

**Copy DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel: "look for a pattern in the existing codebase and build off
that")** — read `EmptyCart` directly
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`) rather than
inventing wording. Its actual structure: an icon, a bold heading, `isRegistered`-branched body copy,
a "Continue Shopping" button (`href="/"`), and — guests only — a second "Sign In" button
(`href="/account"`). Adapted directly for Recently Viewed, same structure, same two CTAs verbatim
(no reason to invent different ones — the destinations and intent are identical):

| Piece | Copy |
|---|---|
| Heading | "You haven't viewed anything yet." |
| Body (registered) | "Continue shopping to start building your history." |
| Body (guest) | "Sign in to keep track of your history, or continue shopping." |
| CTA 1 (both) | "Continue Shopping" → `/` |
| CTA 2 (guest only) | "Sign In" → `/account` |

Icon: `EmptyCart` uses `BasketIcon`; no obvious Recently-Viewed equivalent exists in
`overrides/app/components/icons` — check at implementation time, and omit the icon entirely (heading
+ copy + CTA still satisfies the pattern) rather than force a visually-unrelated one. This is a
real, shippable default now, not a "Jasmijn to confirm" placeholder — still fine for Jasmijn to
revise the wording later, but it does not block the build.

**Indexing (DECIDED 2026-09-06 by Marcel): `noindex, nofollow`.**

**Gotcha — do not use `Seo`'s `noIndex` prop for this.** Base `Seo`
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx:20`) emits
`<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` for that prop — **`noindex` only, no `nofollow`**. It does
accept `children`, which render inside its `<Helmet>`. Pass the directive as a child and leave
`noIndex` unset:

```tsx
<Seo title={...} description={...}>
  <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />
</Seo>
```

Passing both `noIndex` **and** the child would emit two competing `robots` tags whose precedence
depends on Helmet's dedupe order — do not rely on that. Page-level `<Seo>` precedent already exists at
`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`, `experience/index.tsx` and `contentfulPreview/index.tsx`.

- **Empty state renders** (heading + copy + CTA) when there is no history, with the guest variant

- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` clean. `npm run build` matters here specifically: a bad
  `loadable` import path fails at build, not at `tsc`.
- **New mapper (`recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`) pass criteria, added 2026-09-07:** no React, no
  `react-intl`, no hook import (`conventions.md` > Utilities, same rule as A3). Calls base
  `getPriceData`, never hand-rolls list/sale-price comparison. `originalPrice` set only when

10	/**
11	 * Get the human-friendly version of the variation values that users have selected.
12	 * Useful for displaying these values in the UI.
13	 *
14	 * @param {Object} variationAttributes - The products variation attributes.
15	 * @param {Object} values - The variations selected attribute values.
16	 * @returns {Object} - A key value map of the display name and display value.
17	 *
18	 * @example
19	 * const displayValues = getDisplayVariationValues(
20	 *     [ { "id": "color", "name": "Colour", "values": [ { "name": "royal", "orderable": true, "value": "JJ5FUXX" } ] } ],
21	 *     { "color": "JJ5FUXX" }
22	 * )
23	 * // returns { "Colour": "royal" }
24	 */
25	export const getDisplayVariationValues = (variationAttributes, values = {}) => {
26	    if (!variationAttributes || !Array.isArray(variationAttributes)) {
27	        return {}
28	    }
29	
30	    const returnVal = Object.entries(values).reduce((acc, [id, value]) => {
31	        const attribute = variationAttributes.find(({id: attributeId}) => attributeId === id)
32	        if (!attribute || !attribute.values) {
33	            return acc
34	        }
35	
36	        const attributeValue = attribute.values.find(
37	            ({value: attributeValue}) => attributeValue === value
38	        )
39	
40	        if (attributeValue) {
41	            return {
42	                ...acc,
43	                [attribute.name]: attributeValue.name
44	            }

47	    }, {})
48	    return returnVal

51	/**
52	 * Normalizes data for product sets and product bundles into the same format
53	 * Useful for operations that apply to both product sets and product bundles
54	 * Creates deep clones of child products to avoid mutation issues
55	 *
56	 * @param {Object} product - A product set or product bundle
57	 * @returns {Object} - returns normalized product if product is a set/bundle, otherwise returns original product
58	 */
59	export const normalizeSetBundleProduct = (product) => {
60	    if (!product?.type.set && !product?.type.bundle) return product
61	
62	    const childProducts = product?.type.set
63	        ? product.setProducts.map((child) => {
64	              return {
65	                  product: {...child},
66	                  quantity: null
67	              }
68	          })
69	        : product.bundledProducts.map((child) => {
70	              return {
71	                  ...child,
72	                  product: {...child.product}
73	              }
74	          })
75	
76	    return {
77	        ...product,
78	        childProducts
79	    }

92	    const itemsToBeUpdated = []
93	    bundle?.bundledProductItems?.forEach((bundleChild) => {

95	            (childProduct) =>

101

103	        if (childSelection && selectedProductId !== bundleChild.productId) {

114	/**
115	 * This function extract the price information of a given product
116	 * If a product is a master,
117	 *  currentPrice: get the lowest price (including promotional prices) among variants
118	 *  listPrice: get the list price of the variant that has lowest price (including promotional price)
119	 *  maxPrice: the max price in tieredPrices of variant that has lowest price
120	 * @param {object} product - product detail object
121	 * @param {object} opts - options to pass into the function like intl, quantity, and currency
122	 */
123	export const getPriceData = (product, opts = {}) => {
124	    const {quantity = 1} = opts
125	    const isASet = product?.hitType === 'set' || !!product?.type?.set
126	    const isMaster = product?.hitType === 'master' || !!product?.type?.master
127	    let currentPrice
128	    let variantWithLowestPrice
129	    // grab the variant that has the lowest price (including promotional price)
130	    if (isMaster) {
131	        variantWithLowestPrice = findLowestPrice(product)
132	        currentPrice = variantWithLowestPrice?.minPrice
133	    } else {
134	        currentPrice = findLowestPrice(product)?.minPrice
135	    }
136	
137	    // since the price is the lowest value among price books, each product will have at lease a single item tiered price at quantity 1
138	    // the highest value of tieredPrices is presumptively the list price
139	    const tieredPrices = variantWithLowestPrice?.data?.tieredPrices || product?.tieredPrices || []
140	    const maxTieredPrice = tieredPrices?.length
141	        ? Math.max(...tieredPrices.map((item) => item.price))
142	        : undefined
143	    const highestTieredPrice = tieredPrices.find((tier) => tier.price === maxTieredPrice)
144	    const listPrice = highestTieredPrice?.price
145	
146	    // if a product has tieredPrices, get the tiered that has the higher closest quantity to current quantity
147	    const filteredTiered = tieredPrices.filter((tiered) => tiered.quantity <= quantity)
148	    const closestTieredPrice =
149	        filteredTiered.length &&
150	        filteredTiered.reduce((prev, curr) => {
151	            return Math.abs(curr.quantity - quantity) < Math.abs(prev.quantity - quantity)
152	                ? curr
153	                : prev
154	        })
155	    return {
156	        currentPrice,
157	        listPrice,
158	        pricePerUnit: product?.pricePerUnit,
159	        isOnSale: currentPrice < listPrice,
160	        isASet,
161	        isMaster,
162	        // For a product, set price is the lowest price of its children, so the price should be considered a range
163	        // For a master product, when it has more than 2 variants, we use the lowest priced variant, so it is  considered a range price

165	        isRange: (isMaster && product?.variants?.length > 1) || isASet || false,
166	        // priceMax is for product set
167	        tieredPrice: closestTieredPrice?.price,

202	            : () => true
203	
204	    return imageGroups?.filter(typeFilter)?.filter(attributeFilter)
205	}
206	
207	/**
208	 * Provided a product this function will return the variation attibutes decorated with
209	 * `href` and `swatch` image for the given attribute values. This allows easier access
210	 * when creating components that commonly use this information.
211	 *
212	 * @param {Product} product
213	 * @param {object} opts
214	 * @param {string} opts.swatchViewType - The `viewTypeId` for the swatch image. Defaults to `swatch`.
215	 *
216	 * @returns {VariationAttributes[]} decoratedVariationAttributes
217	 */
218	export const getDecoratedVariationAttributes = (product, opts = {}) => {
219	    const swatchViewType = opts.swatchViewType || 'swatch'
220	
221	    return product?.variationAttributes?.map((variationAttribute) => ({
222	        ...variationAttribute,
223	        values: variationAttribute.values.map((value) => {
224	            const variationValues = {[variationAttribute.id]: value.value}
225	
226	            return {
227	                ...value,
228	                swatch: filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups, {
229	                    viewType: swatchViewType,
230	                    variationValues
231	                })?.[0]?.images[0],
232	                href: rebuildPathWithParams(
233	                    productUrlBuilder({id: product.productId}),
234	                    variationValues
235	                )
236	            }
237	        })
238	    }))
239	}
240	
241	/**
242	 * Find the lowest price of a product, across all of its price books and promotions
243	 * @param {Object} product - product data from the API
244	 * @returns {Object|undefined} the lowest price for the given product. If it's a promotional price, the promotion will also be returned.
245	 */
246	export const findLowestPrice = (product) => {
247	    if (!product) return
248	
249	    // Look at all of the variants, only if it's a master product.
250	    // i.e. when a shopper has narrowed down to a variant, do not look into other variants
251	    const isMaster = product.hitType === 'master' || !!product.type?.master
252	    if (isMaster && !product.variants) {
253	        console.warn(
254	            'Expecting `product.variants` to exist. For more accuracy, please tweak your API request to ask for the variants details.'
255	        )
256	    }
257	    const array = isMaster && product.variants ? product.variants : [product]
258	
259	    const res = array.reduce(
260	        (prev, data) => {
261	            const promotions = data.productPromotions || []
262	            const [smallestPromotionalPrice, promo] = getSmallestValByProperty(
263	                promotions,
264	                'promotionalPrice'
265	            )
266	
267	            let salePrice = data.price
268	            let promotion = null
269	            if (smallestPromotionalPrice && smallestPromotionalPrice < data.price) {
270	                salePrice = smallestPromotionalPrice
271	                promotion = promo
272	            }
273	
274	            return salePrice < prev.minPrice ? {minPrice: salePrice, promotion, data} : prev
275	        },
276	        {minPrice: Infinity, promotion: null, data: null}
277	    )
278	    return {
279	        ...res,
280	        // when minPrice is infinity, meaning there is no variant with lowest price found, we rest the value to 0 as minPrice to be able to use this value on UI
281	        minPrice: res.minPrice === Infinity ? 0 : res.minPrice
282	    }
283	}
284	
285	/**
286	 * @private
287	 * Find the smallest value by key from a given array
288	 * @returns {Array} an array of such smallest value and the item containing this value
289	 * @example
290	 * const [value, itemContainingValue] = getSmallestValByProperty(array, key)
291	 */
292	const getSmallestValByProperty = (arr, key) => {
293	    if (!arr || !arr.length) return []
294	    if (!key) {
295	        throw new Error('Please specify a key.')
296	    }
297	    const filtered = arr.filter((item) => {
298	        const value = item[key]
299	        return value === 0 || value === '0' ? true : Number(value)
300	    })
301	    if (filtered.length === 0) return []
302	
303	    return filtered.reduce(
304	        (prev, item) => {
305	            const value = item[key]
306	            const [prevValue] = prev
307	            return value < prevValue ? [value, item] : prev
308	        },
309	        [Infinity, null]
310	    )
311	}

import React from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../zimmProductCard';

export type ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps = {
  /**
   * Typed as `ReactNode`, not `string` — this component owns no copy/intl, the same discipline
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title` prop documents for itself (build plan §A5/§B1). Styled
   * with `textStyle="heading3"` directly below, applied from the start rather than left for a
   * caller to pre-style — the rail's own `title` shipped once *without* this and had to be fixed
   * after live Storybook testing caught it rendering in the ambient body weight instead of the
   * intended one (see `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`'s own docblock, "Styling resolved
   * 2026-09-08"). That token is independently confirmed correct for THIS component's own title
   * bar too, not just carried over from the rail: build plan §B1's `get_variable_defs` read on
   * Figma node `3332:37131` ("PLP Bar desktop") returns "Default/Heading 3" — Futura Round
   * Medium, size 16 / line-height 18 / letterSpacing -1 — cross-checked against
   * `theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s own registered `heading3` (`fontSizes.xs` 16px /
   * `lineHeights['2xs']` 18px / `letterSpacings.xs` -0.12px, the same documented sub-pixel
   * rounding `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s Units section already carries elsewhere /
   * `textTransform: uppercase` already baked in) and found to match exactly.
   */
  title: ReactNode;
  /**
   * A pre-formatted, already-pluralized node (e.g. "16 Items" / "1 Item") — this component does
   * not own copy/intl, matching `title` above and `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own container/
   * presentational split (`.claude/rules/components.md`). Build plan §B1: the item count is
   * mechanical ICU-plural-selector copy ("go for it" — Marcel, 2026-09-08), which is the calling
   * container's job (SFCC-84's Full History page container, not built by this step), not this
   * organism's. **Rendered exactly as received — never recomputed from `cards.length` here.** A
   * caller is expected to derive this from the same `cards` array it passes below; see this
   * component's own stories/tests for the "the two stay in sync when a real caller wires them
   * together correctly" proof this step's brief asked for — that proof lives at the call site
   * (story/test), not as internal recomputation, precisely so a future divergence between what a
   * caller *says* the count is and what actually rendered stays visible instead of being silently
   * papered over by this component re-deriving its own "correct" answer.
   *
   * Same `textStyle="heading3"` / colour treatment as `title` above — confirmed via the same
   * `3332:37131` screenshot, which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) and "16 ITEMS" (right) in the
   * same text style.
   */
  itemCountLabel: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Rendered in the exact order received — no sorting or reordering happens here, and (unlike
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) no cap/slice either: SFCC-84's Full History page has no ordering AC
   * of its own, but per build plan §B1 "the page is the rail's overflow — same order or it reads
   * as broken", and the page container (not this component) is already responsible for capping
   * its fetch at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (24, `app/constants/index.ts`) before this
   * component ever sees `cards` — see the build plan's B2 step. Typed as the full
   * `ZimmProductCardProps` union, matching `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own contract verbatim
   * (build plan §A5) rather than a variation-narrowed type, so this component spreads each entry
   * straight into `ZimmProductCard` rather than forcing a variation onto every card itself. In
   * real usage every entry already carries `variation: 'plp'` by construction — SFCC-84 AC 2 /
   * SFCC-236's own "Recently Viewed Full History variation (same behavior as PLP card)" AC block,
   * corroborated 2026-09-07/08 against the `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's own
   * "Recently Viewed (Full History)" section, which renders `variation: 'plp'` cards with zero
   * different props from its own PLP demo cards (see this component's own recipe file for the
   * full citation). Nothing new was needed on `ZimmProductCard` itself for this — see that
   * component's own module docblock: *"'Recently Viewed Full History' is not a fourth
   * variation... callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it."*
   */
  cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[];
};

const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid';

/**
 * SFCC-84 — the Recently Viewed Full History grid organism (build plan section B1). Purely
 * presentational: data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — the
 * same container/presentational split `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (SFCC-83, build plan §A5) already
 * establishes, adapted here from a horizontally-scrolling rail to a 4-up desktop grid. The
 * container (build plan §B2, not built by this step) is responsible for reading the shopper's
 * tracked view history, fetching real product data for it, mapping the result to `plp`-shaped
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` (a new mapper, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — NOT
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, whose narrower image-only output cannot
 * feed this grid's fuller `plp` card), and supplying `title`/`itemCountLabel` copy.
 *
 * **Design source, stated plainly per build plan §B1: this grid's layout comes from a
 * PROVISIONAL design source** (`Zimmermann_Designs` file, node `3332:35655` — not a PDP/Recently
 * Viewed node in the authoritative `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file the rail sibling uses;
 * see Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule, restated verbatim in the build plan). That ranking is
 * unchanged by anything below. What DID change, this session (2026-09-07/08): the specific
 * geometry/typography/variation values actually used here were independently verified, not taken
 * on the provisional source's word alone —
 *   - **Layout** confirmed via live Figma metadata AND a real screenshot of `3332:37131` ("PLP
 *     Bar desktop", 1440×75), which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) / "16 ITEMS" (right) —
 *     confirming both the title-left/count-right layout and the title bar's own content in one
 *     node, not inferred from layer names alone (which the build plan notes were misleading here).
 *   - **The `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`) child holds four stacked `Products Module Desktop` instances**
 *     (`35665`/`35666`/`35668`/`35669`, each 1440×606) — two of which were checked directly and are
 *     structurally identical (four `Products S Desktop` instances each, 288×542, at
 *     x=0/384/768/1152): confirmed as 4 repeated example rows of real content, not 4 different
 *     states to design against.
 *   - **The `variation: 'plp'` decision** (see `cards`' own JSDoc above) is independently
 *     corroborated by a real, interactive prior-art branch, not just an AC-text reading — see this
 *     recipe file's own docblock for the full citation.
 *   - **The 96px horizontal card gap** (this recipe's own `GRID_CARD_GAP`) was checked at two
 *     independent Figma sources specifically because it does NOT resolve to any bound variable —
 *     see this recipe's own docblock for the full "RESOLVED... checked twice, genuinely
 *     un-tokenised" citation.
 * So: provisional design *source*, independently confirmed design *values* — both things are true
 * at once, and this docblock states both rather than letting the provisional-source caveat imply
 * the specific numbers below are unverified guesses, or letting the confirmed-values framing imply
 * the source ranking has changed.
 *
 * **This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`**
 * (a deliberate build-plan call, not an oversight): the rail's header is Figma node
 * `40000538:20306` (h96/h56); this grid's is `3332:37131` (h75, one Desktop reading only, no
 * separate Tablet/Mobile node). Different components in Figma, so sharing would be a wrong DRY
 * call — see this recipe's own docblock for why no fixed header height is set here at all (unlike
 * the rail's own two-tier `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`).
 *
 * Renders `null` for an empty `cards` array — the same defensive-leaf-component default
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` uses (its own container owns the actual "should this exist at all"
 * decision; SFCC-84's Full History page has its own separate empty-state design, per build plan
 * §B2, which does not involve mounting this component with zero cards at all).
 */
export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = ({ title, itemCountLabel, cards }: ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE, {});

  if (cards.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid">
      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
          {title}
        </chakra.span>
        <chakra.span
          textStyle="heading3"
          color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"
          data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-count"
        >
          {itemCountLabel}
        </chakra.span>
      </chakra.div>
      <chakra.div __css={styles.grid} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-group">
        {cards.map((card) => (
          <ZimmProductCard key={card.id} {...card} />
        ))}
      </chakra.div>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

Both new files are clean — no `console.log`, no React/react-intl import, no actual `any` type usage (all `any` mentions are in docblock prose explaining the untyped external module boundary), no non-null assertions.

## Summary

**Files created** (exactly the two named in the task, nothing else touched):
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts`

### What the mapper does

`selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard(product, formatPrice)` maps a plain Commerce API `Product` (`ShopperProductsTypes.Product`, the exact shape `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` produces) to `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` — badge, size chips, was/now pricing, multi-image gallery, with `headingLevel: 'h3'` and `variation: 'plp'` baked in directly (confirmed types by reading `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` directly). It is a pure module — no React/react-intl import, `formatPrice` injected as a parameter, same as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`.

- **Price fix (the core ask):** `selectPriceFields` calls base `getPriceData(product)` once (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:123-170`, read directly) and derives both `currentPrice` and `originalPrice` from that single call's `currentPrice`/`listPrice`/`isOnSale`. `originalPrice` is only set when `isOnSale` is true. Neither field ever reads a flat `product.price` separately.
- **Multi-image:** `selectGalleryImages` is a near-verbatim port of `productListCardMapper.ts`'s function (same "largest group wins, viewpoint-agnostic" heuristic), re-pointed at `product.imageGroups` directly.
- **Primary image:** not ported from `productListCardMapper.ts` (that reads a Search-hit-only flat `image` field that doesn't exist on plain `Product`). Instead mirrors `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectPrimaryImage` (medium-viewType lookup, required non-empty `alt`), since that file already solved this exact problem for this exact input shape.
- **Size chips:** `selectSizeChipValues` ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes`.
- **Hard gate:** returns `null` for no usable name or no usable image, never throws — same contract as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`.

### Badge-field finding (as requested)

Confirmed by reading `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:59783-59835` directly (the block backing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`): **there is no typed `c_productBadges` field on the plain `Product` type** — only a generic `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, which would let `product.c_productBadges` compile without error but proves nothing about whether it's actually populated. `c_productBadges` is confirmed real only on `ShopperSearchTypes.ProductSearchHit` (the Search-index endpoint `productListCardMapper.ts` reads it from). The plain `getProducts` endpoint `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` calls is a hydration endpoint, not the search-index endpoint, and requests no expand parameter suggesting custom attributes are included. **I left `badge: undefined`** rather than guess — this is a real, unresolved gap, not a design choice, and needs a live check against a real badged product in a running environment before it can be filled in.

### Autonomous decisions (precedent-based, not stopped on)

1. **Included `headingLevel: 'h3'` and `variation: 'plp'` as literals in the output** (unlike `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, which excludes both as its container's job) — matching `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `ProductListCardResult` pattern instead, per the task's explicit "matching what productListCardMapper.ts already produces." **This was corroborated after the fact**: while investigating the current branch state I found `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx` (B1, already built though uncommitted) already documents that its `cards` prop expects fully-baked `ZimmProductCardProps` spread directly into `<ZimmProductCard {...card} />`, and states "in real usage every entry already carries `variation: 'plp'` by construction" — confirming this shape is exactly what B2's not-yet-built container will need.
2. **Did not map `isUnavailable`/`onNotifyMe`/`onAddToBag`/`hoverImage`.** Not in the task's explicit feature list (badge, size chips, was/now, multi-image) or Jasmijn's AC quote ("image, name, badge, price incl. was/now, and cart icon"); all are optional, and correctly deriving master-vs-variant availability is a distinct problem this task didn't ask me to solve.
3. **Local type aliases (`RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct`, `FormatPrice`) instead of importing from `recentlyViewedCard.ts`** — keeps this a genuinely separate, self-contained module, matching the task's explicit "port, don't import" instruction extended consistently to types, not just functions.
4. **`RawImage` aliases the real `ShopperProductsTypes.Image` SDK type** rather than hand-rolling a duplicate shape the way `productListCardMapper.ts` did — per AGENTS.md's Type Definitions rule.
5. **Added a named `SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID` constant** for the `'size'` literal (ported function used it inline) — conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule, a small improvement scoped only to my own new file.
6. **`getPriceData`'s return narrowed to a local `SfccPriceData` type** rather than propagating the implicit `any` from the untyped vendor module — matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s established pattern for the same untyped function.
7. **Exported `selectGalleryImages`/`selectSizeChipValues` (ported from `productListCardMapper.ts`, which exports both) but kept `selectPrimaryImage`/`selectPriceFields` private** (matching `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, which keeps its analogous `selectPrimaryImage` private) — each ported piece follows its own precedent's export surface.
